title: Erdős Problem #28: The Erdős–Turán Conjecture on Additive Bases
description: If A ⊆ ℕ is an additive basis of order 2 (A+A covers all but finitely many integers), must the representation function r(n) be unbounded? $500 bounty. Status: OPEN.

meta.assumptions: 2 axioms: grekos_lower_bound (Grekos et al. 2003: r_A(n) ≥ 6 infinitely often), borwein_lower_bound (Borwein et al.: r_A(n) ≥ 8 infinitely often). sidon_not_basis PROVED as theorem (PR #6840). sidon_density_bound PROVED via bridge lemma importing Erdos340.sidon_upper_bound_weak. 14 theorems proved including isAsymptoticBasis_iff, sidon_repFunc_bounded, erdos_turan_holds_for_nat, basis_element_count_sq, sidon_density_bound.
prerequisites: Basic analytic number theory (Fourier analysis on integers)
Asymptotic notation and density of integer sets

mathlibDependencies.description: Cardinality of sets as natural numbers
Subsets of finite sets are finite

originalContributions: Complete formal framework for the Erdős–Turán conjecture: representation functions, asymptotic bases, Sidon sets, and counting functions
Proved isAsymptoticBasis_iff: equivalence of two basis definitions (threshold vs finite complement)
Proved sidon_repFunc_bounded: Sidon sets have representation ≤ 2 (original proof via pair-matching argument)

sections.title: Header and Imports
sections.summary: Module docstring stating the conjecture and its $500 bounty, Mathlib imports, namespace opens.
sections.mathContext: Erdos-Turan conjecture: if $A + A \supseteq \{N_0, N_0+1, \ldots\}$, then $\limsup_{n \to \infty} r_A(n) = \infty$ where $r_A(n) = |\{(a,b) \in A^2 : a+b=n\}|$.

sections.title: Part I: Representation Function
sections.summary: Ordered and unordered representation functions: r_A(n) counts pairs (a,b) in A×A with a+b=n.

sections.title: Part II: Sumset and Asymptotic Basis
sections.summary: Sumset definition, Sidon set predicate (IsSidon), asymptotic basis of order 2 (IsAsymptoticBasis), and finiteness lemmas.
sections.mathContext: $A + A = \{a+b : a,b \in A\}$ (Minkowski sum). IsSidon: $r_A(n) \leq 1$ for all $n$. IsAsymptoticBasis: $|\mathbb{N} \setminus (A+A)| < \infty$.

sections.title: Part III: Basic Properties
sections.summary: Proved lemmas: Sidon representation bound (r_A(n) ≤ 2), exact computation of r_ℕ(n), and helper lemmas.
sections.mathContext: IsSidon $A \Rightarrow r_A(n) \leq 2$ (ordered count). For $A = \mathbb{N}$: $r_{\mathbb{N}}(n) = n + 1$ (ordered pairs $(a, n-a)$ for $0 \leq a \leq n$).

sections.title: Part IV: The Main Conjecture
sections.summary: Weak form (limsup r_A(n) = ∞) and strong form (limsup r_A(n)/log n > 0), plus the official Problem #28 definition.
sections.mathContext: Weak: $\forall k,\; \exists n: r_A(n) > k$. Strong: $\exists c > 0,\; \forall M,\; \exists n > M: r_A(n) > c \log n$.

sections.title: Part V: Known Partial Results
sections.summary: Grekos et al. (2003): r_A(n) ≥ 6 i.o. Borwein et al.: r_A(n) ≥ 8 i.o.
sections.mathContext: Best known: $\exists$ infinitely many $n$ with $r_A(n) \geq 8$ (Borwein et al.). Previously: $r_A(n) \geq 6$ i.o. (Grekos et al. 2003). The conjecture requires $r_A(n) \to \infty$.

sections.title: Part VI: Examples
sections.summary: ℕ as a basis, computation of r_ℕ(n) = n/2+1 or (n+1)/2, Finset-to-Set conversion lemmas.
sections.mathContext: $r_{\mathbb{N}}(2k) = k+1$ and $r_{\mathbb{N}}(2k+1) = k+1$ (unordered). Demonstrates $\mathbb{N}$ is an asymptotic basis of order 2 trivially ($\mathbb{N} + \mathbb{N} = \mathbb{N}$) with unbounded $r$.

sections.title: Part VII: Connection to Sidon Sets
sections.summary: The most substantial section: proves `sidon_density_bound` (Sidon sets have $\leq \sqrt{2N}+1$ elements in $[1,N]$) via bridge to Erdős #340, then proves `sidon_not_basis` as a full theorem (not axiom) via a combinatorial counting argument. Four private helper lemmas (`isSidon_set_to_finset`, `card_upper_triangle`, `finset_sumset_eq_upper_image`, `finset_sumset_card_bound`) build the infrastructure. The `sidon_not_basis` proof chooses $T = 4N_0 + 100$, $N = T^2$, bounds $|A \cap [0,N]| \leq 5N_0 + 126$ via the Sidon density bound, then shows the sumset of this restricted set is too small to cover $[N_0, N]$ — a contradiction from $2(4N_0+100)^2 + 2 \leq (5N_0+126)(5N_0+127) + 2N_0$ being impossible for all $N_0 \geq 0$.
sections.mathContext: Sidon density: $|A \cap [1,N]| \leq \sqrt{2N} + 1$. For basis $A$ with threshold $N_0$: set $S = A \cap [0, T^2]$ with $T = 4N_0+100$. Then $|\text{sumset}(S)| \cdot 2 \leq |S|(|S|+1)$ (upper-triangle counting), but coverage requires $|\text{sumset}(S)| \geq T^2 - N_0 + 1$. The Sidon bound $|S| \leq 5N_0+126$ forces $2(T^2 - N_0 + 1) \leq (5N_0+126)(5N_0+127)$, which fails since $32N_0^2 + 1600N_0 + 20002 \leq 25N_0^2 + 1267N_0 + 16002$ is impossible.

sections.title: Part VIII: Ordered vs Unordered Representations
sections.summary: Proved: r_A(n) ≥ r_A^≤(n) since unordered pairs are a subset of ordered pairs.
sections.mathContext: $r_A(n) \geq r_A^{\leq}(n)$ since $\{(a,b) : a \leq b, a+b=n\} \subseteq \{(a,b) : a+b=n\}$. The ordered count double-counts pairs with $a \neq b$.

sections.title: Part IX: Conjecture Holds for ℕ
sections.summary: Proved: the Erdős–Turán conjecture holds trivially for A = ℕ, since r_ℕ(2k+2) = k+2 > k.
sections.mathContext: For $A = \mathbb{N}$: $r_{\mathbb{N}}(2k+2) = k+2 > k$ for all $k$, so $\limsup r_{\mathbb{N}}(n) = \infty$. This is the trivial case — the conjecture's difficulty lies in sparse bases.

sections.title: Part X: Basis Density Lower Bound
sections.summary: Proved: any basis A satisfies |A ∩ [0,N]|² ≥ N - N₀ + 1, giving |A ∩ [0,N]| ≥ c√N.

overview.historicalContext: Paul Erdős and Pál Turán posed this conjecture in their landmark 1941 paper 'On a problem of Sidon in additive number theory and some related problems' (J. London Math. Soc.), which also introduced the systematic study of $B_2$ sequences. The conjecture emerged from their investigation of how the representation function $r_A(n)$ behaves for additive bases — sets $A$ whose sumset $A + A$ covers all sufficiently large integers. Erdős attached a $500 bounty, one of his largest prizes, signaling its depth within additive combinatorics. Key partial results include the Erdős–Fuchs theorem (1956), which proved that cumulative representations must fluctuate (sharpened by Montgomery and Vaughan in 1990 to the optimal exponent $1/4$), and the Halberstam–Roth observation that average representations diverge. The conjecture connects to a web of related problems: Problem #40 on $B_2[g]$ sets, the structure theory of Sidon sets (initiated by Simon Sidon in the 1930s), and Waring-type problems on additive bases of higher order. Despite 85 years of effort by leaders in additive combinatorics — including Nathanson, Cilleruelo, and Lev — even the basic conjecture remains completely open.
overview.problemStatement: If $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ and $A + A$ contains all but finitely many natural numbers, must $\limsup_{n \to \infty} r_A(n) = \infty$, where $r_A(n) = |\{(a,b) \in A \times A : a + b = n, \; a \leq b\}|$?
overview.text: A 647-line formalization of Erdős Problem #28 (\$500 bounty, OPEN since 1941) that builds the complete framework for the Erdős–Turán conjecture on additive bases. Defines the representation function $r_A(n)$ (ordered and unordered), the asymptotic basis predicate, and the counting function $A(N)$, then states the conjecture in three tiers: weak ($\limsup r_A(n) = \infty$), strong ($\limsup r_A(n)/\log n > 0$), and density version ($A(N) \geq c\sqrt{N}$ suffices). The 2 axioms encode known partial results: Grekos et al. (2003): $r_A(n) \geq 6$ i.o., and Borwein et al.: $r_A(n) \geq 8$ i.o. The `sidon_not_basis` result — that infinite Sidon sets cannot be asymptotic bases — is now fully proved as a theorem (not an axiom) via a combinatorial counting argument using the Sidon density bound imported from Erdős #340. The 14 proved theorems include `isAsymptoticBasis_iff` (equivalence of basis definitions), `sidon_repFunc_bounded` ($r_A(n) \leq 2$ for Sidon sets), `sidon_not_basis` (Sidon sets too sparse for bases), `erdos_turan_holds_for_nat` (conjecture holds trivially for $A = \mathbb{N}$), and `basis_element_count_sq` (density lower bound $A(N)^2 \geq N - N_0 + 1$).
overview.proofStrategy:
We formalize the core objects of the conjecture — the representation function $r_A(n)$, the asymptotic basis condition $(A+A)^c$ finite, and the counting function $A(N) = |A \cap [1,N]|$ — then state the main conjecture and two strengthenings as axioms. The Lean file is organized in ten parts:

1. **Definitions** (Part I): `repFunction`, `IsAsymptoticBasis2`, `countingFn`
2. **Main conjecture** (Part IV): stated as `axiom erdos_turan_conjecture`
3. **Basis density** (Part II): proved `basis_counting_lower` (A(N) ≥ √N/2 − 1) via sumset counting — every n ∈ [T+1,N] lies in the image of F×F, so N−T ≤ |F|²
4. **Sidon connection** (Part VII): proved `sidon_not_basis` and `erdos_40_from_28` from the axiom; imported `Erdos340.sidon_upper_bound_weak` for the density bound
5. **Partial results** (Part V): axiomatized Grekos et al. 2003 ($r_A \geq 6$ i.o.) and Borwein et al. 2006 ($r_A \geq 8$ i.o.); proved Erdős–Fuchs fluctuation and Halberstam–Roth average divergence as theorems from the conjecture
6. **ℕ special case** (Part IX): proved `conjecture_holds_nat` — the full conjecture holds when $A = \mathbb{N}$ itself (trivial but illustrative)
7. **Density lower bound** (Part X): proved a quantitative lower bound on basis density
keyInsights: **No thin basis can exist**: The conjecture asserts that controlling $r_A(n) \leq C$ is fundamentally incompatible with $A + A$ covering all large integers — a profound structural constraint on sumsets

**Logarithmic growth from probabilistic heuristics**: For a 'random' set of density $\sim \sqrt{N}$, each $r_A(n)$ has expectation $\sim \log n$, suggesting $\limsup r_A(n)/\log n > 0$ as the natural quantitative form

**Erdős–Fuchs falls short**: The cumulative sum $\sum r_A(n)$ must oscillate by $\Omega(N^{1/4}/\sqrt{\log N})$, but these fluctuations could concentrate in a few large terms without any single $r_A(n)$ being large — a subtle gap between average and pointwise behavior

**Sidon sets confirm the extremal case**: Sets with $r \leq 1$ (Sidon/$B_2$ sets) satisfy $A(N) \leq \sqrt{N} + O(N^{1/4})$, which is too sparse for a basis, confirming the conjecture vacuously at the boundary

**Hierarchy of related problems**: #28 implies #40 ($B_2[g]$ sets cannot be bases), connects to #1145 on dense $B_2[g]$ constructions, and motivates the density version that weakens the basis hypothesis to $A(N) \gg \sqrt{N}$

**Density gap separating bases from bounded-representation sets**: The basis density lower bound $|A \cap [1,N]| \geq c\sqrt{N - N_0}$ (proved as `basis_element_count_sq` in this entry) is exactly the threshold where bounded representations become impossible. Any set achieving the basis density $\sqrt{N}$ has on average $\sqrt{N} \cdot \sqrt{N} / N = \Theta(1)$ representations per integer — the *minimum* density that can cover $\mathbb{N}$. Conversely, Ruzsa's 1998 construction of an infinite Sidon set with density $\sim N^{\sqrt{2}-1} \approx N^{0.414}$ — the densest known representation-bounded set — falls strictly below the $N^{1/2}$ basis threshold. The conjecture asserts this density gap (between $N^{0.414}$ and $N^{0.5}$) cannot be bridged by any clever construction with bounded $r_A(n)$ — a structural rigidity that no current technique (probabilistic, Fourier-analytic, or combinatorial) can establish.
prerequisites: Basic analytic number theory (Fourier analysis on integers)
Asymptotic notation and density of integer sets

conclusion.summary: This formalization captures the full landscape of the Erdős–Turán conjecture on additive bases: the core definitions, the main conjecture and its strengthenings, connections to Sidon sets and Problem #40, and the partial results (Erdős–Fuchs, Halberstam–Roth) that illuminate why the problem is so hard. The gap between what is known (average representations diverge, cumulative sums oscillate) and what is conjectured (individual representations are unbounded) highlights a deep open question about the pointwise behavior of additive structure.
conclusion.implications:
**Theoretical Significance**: A proof would establish that no additive basis of order 2 can have uniformly bounded representations — a fundamental dichotomy in additive number theory.

This would resolve Problem #40 as a corollary, settle the structure of $B_2[g]$ sets relative to bases, and likely introduce new techniques at the intersection of additive combinatorics and analytic number theory. The density version, if true, would extend the result far beyond bases to any sufficiently dense set.
openQuestions: Can the Erdős–Fuchs fluctuation theorem be strengthened to imply pointwise unboundedness of $r_A(n)$, or is there a fundamental barrier?
Does the conjecture hold under the weaker density hypothesis $A(N) \geq c\sqrt{N}$, without assuming $A + A$ covers almost all integers?
What is the correct growth rate: is $\limsup r_A(n)/\log n > 0$, or could representations grow slower than logarithmically?
Can Fourier-analytic or circle-method techniques (as used in Waring's problem) be adapted to attack this conjecture?

crossReferences.description: Problem #1 (distinct subset sums) and Problem #28 (unbounded representation) are dual questions in additive combinatorics: #1 asks when all subset sums are distinct ($r \leq 1$), while #28 asks whether representation counts must be unbounded for bases. Both concern the fundamental tension between density and additive structure

Both bear the name Erdős-Turán and concern how arithmetic structure is forced by density. Problem #3 asks whether dense sets must contain APs; Problem #28 asks whether bases must have unbounded representations. Both remain open after 80+ years

Problem #39 on infinite Sidon set growth asks about the maximum growth rate of Sidon sets ($r_A(n) \leq 1$). Sidon sets are precisely the extremal case for Problem #28: they have minimal representation but are provably too sparse to be bases

Problem #41 on $B_h$ sequence density bounds generalizes Sidon sets to higher-order representation constraints. The Erdős-Turán conjecture on bases of order 2 connects directly to whether $B_2[g]$ sets can be bases — Problem #28 implies they cannot
Problem #42 on Sidon sets with disjoint difference sets explores the structure theory of $B_2$ sets, the same objects whose density limitations make the Erdős-Turán conjecture plausible

Problem #40 (also Erdős-Turán): $B_2[g]$ sets cannot be bases. The Lean file proves this as a direct corollary (`erdos_40_from_28`): if $r_A(n) \leq g$ for all $n$, then the Erdős-Turán conjecture forces $r_A(n) > g$ for some $n$, contradiction

Direct Lean dependency: this file imports Proofs.Erdos340GreedySidon to use sidon_upper_bound_weak in the proof of sidon_density_bound. The Sidon density bound ($|A \cap [1,N]| \leq \sqrt{2N}+1$) is a key ingredient in showing Sidon sets cannot be bases

Lagrange's four squares theorem shows the squares form an additive basis of order 4. The Erdős–Turán conjecture asks about bases of order 2 — both concern the structure of additive bases but at different orders, and Lagrange's result motivated the general study of Waring-type additive bases

Erdős Problem #35 concerns Schnirelmann density and additive bases — the Schnirelmann density criterion is the classical tool for proving sets are additive bases. The Erdős-Turán conjecture concerns the representation function of bases rather than their density.

Erdős Problem #29 asks for explicit economical additive bases: sets $A$ with $A + A \supseteq \mathbb{N}$ but $r_A(n)$ growing as slowly as possible. This is the constructive complement to the Erdős-Turán conjecture, which asserts no basis can keep $r_A(n)$ bounded.

Erdős Problem #322 concerns representations as sums of $k$-th powers — a Waring-type generalization of the additive basis question. The Erdős-Turán conjecture specializes to order-2 bases; Waring's problem asks about higher-order bases formed by perfect powers.

Erdős Problem #14 concerns unique sums and non-unique representations in sumsets — the complementary question to Erdős-Turán: while the conjecture asks whether representations must grow, Problem #14 studies when representations can be kept unique.

Erdős–Sárközy conjecture (#1145) asks the same question for two-set bases A + B: if A + B covers all large integers and aₙ/bₙ → 1, must r_{A,B}(n) be unbounded? A direct generalization of #28's theme.

references.note: Sidon's original paper introducing what are now called Sidon sets ($B_2$ sequences) — sets of integers with all pairwise sums distinct, equivalently $r_A(n) \leq 1$. Erdős and Turán's 1941 paper that posed Problem #28 was titled 'On a problem of Sidon...' — the question of whether Sidon sets can be additive bases is the extremal case that motivated the conjecture. Sidon sets remain the only known explicit family certified to be too sparse to be bases.

references.title: Sidon sets in $\mathbb{N}^d$
references.venue: Journal of Combinatorial Theory, Series A, vol. 117, pp. 857–871
references.note: Modern reference on $d$-dimensional Sidon sets and their density bounds. Cilleruelo's work, alongside that of Lev and others, represents the active research frontier in additive combinatorics directly relevant to Problem #28: the structure of sets with bounded representation functions. The density bound $|A \cap [1,N]| \leq \sqrt{N} + O(N^{1/4})$ for Sidon sets (which is used in the gallery proof of `sidon_density_bound`) builds on this line of work.

references.title: An infinite Sidon sequence
references.venue: Journal of Number Theory, vol. 68, pp. 63–71
references.note: Constructs an explicit infinite Sidon sequence with density $|A \cap [1, N]| \gtrsim N^{\sqrt{2}-1}$, currently the densest known infinite Sidon set construction. This sets the upper bound on how dense a representation-bounded set can be — still well below the $\sqrt{N}$ density needed to be a basis, illustrating why the Erdős–Turán conjecture is consistent with all known constructions of additive sets with bounded representation.
